sections.name: Why Hospitals Still Use Leeches
lines: In the 1800s, doctors were so obsessed with leeches that France imported tens of millions of them a year.
They put them on almost everything. Headaches, fevers, even bad moods.
A leech has three tiny jaws with rows of teeth, and its spit is full of chemicals that stop blood from clotting.
And that's why hospitals still use them today. After a surgeon reattaches a finger or an ear, the veins can clog with blood.
A leech drains the extra blood, and keeps it flowing while the veins heal.
In 2004, the US even approved leeches as an official medical device.
